The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal

### /app/gaitmod/stride.rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative 'treeio'

module Walkbay
  FOLD = '/app/livefold'
  SNAP = '/app/snapurn/seals'
  SCRATCH = '/app/inkvat/delta.lst'

  module_function

  def newest
    Dir.children(SNAP).sort.last
  end

  def prior
    kids = Dir.children(SNAP).sort
    kids.length >= 2 ? kids[-2] : kids[-1]
  end

  def loom
    a = File.join(SNAP, prior)
    b = File.join(SNAP, newest)
    changed = []
    (Treeio.files(a) | Treeio.files(b)).each do |rel|
      pa = File.join(a, rel)
      pb = File.join(b, rel)
      same = File.file?(pa) && File.file?(pb) && Treeio.digest(pa) == Treeio.digest(pb)
      next if same

      changed << rel if File.file?(pa) || File.file?(pb)
    end
    File.write(SCRATCH, changed.map { |r| "seal:#{r}" }.join("\n"))
    File.write(SCRATCH, File.read(SCRATCH) + "\n") unless changed.empty?
    changed
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'digest'
require 'find'

module Treeio
  module_function

  def files(root)
    out = []
    return out unless Dir.exist?(root)

    Find.find(root) do |p|
      next unless File.file?(p)

      rel = p.sub(%r{\A#{Regexp.escape(root)}/?}, '')
      next if rel.empty? || rel.start_with?('.')

      out << rel
    end
    out.sort
  end

  def digest(path)
    Digest::SHA256.file(path).hexdigest
  end
end
### /app/joincue/latch.rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'json'
require_relative 'sheets'

module Bindpit
  SCRATCH = '/app/inkvat/delta.lst'
  ROSTER = '/app/inkvat/pick.json'
  LEDGER = '/app/inkvat/sieve.bin'

  module_function

  def hitch
    raw = File.exist?(SCRATCH) ? File.read(SCRATCH) : ''
    tokens = raw.split
    maps = Sheets.load
    rows = []
    tokens.each do |tok|
      rel = tok.sub(/\A(live|seal):/, '')
      key = File.basename(rel)
      assays = []
      maps.each do |mrel, names|
        assays.concat(names) if File.basename(mrel) == key
      end
      assays = assays.uniq.sort
      next if assays.empty?

      rows << { 'path' => "live:#{rel}", 'assays' => assays }
    end
    File.write(ROSTER, JSON.pretty_generate({ 'rows' => rows }) + "\n")
    buf = +''.b
    rows.each do |r|
      pb = r['path'].encode('UTF-8')
      buf << [pb.bytesize].pack('n') << pb
      buf << [r['assays'].length].pack('n')
      r['assays'].each do |a|
        ab = a.encode('UTF-8')
        buf << [ab.bytesize].pack('n') << ab
      end
    end
    File.binwrite(LEDGER, buf)
    rows
  end
end

Analysis: The root cause is confirmed: `gaitmod/stride.rb` compares the two newest snapshots and emits `seal:` tokens instead of comparing `/app/livefold` with newest snapshot and emitting `live:` tokens. The live desk differs from `n1` only at `lib/tax.rb`, which has two assays. Additional correctness defects are present: coverage joining uses basenames rather than exact relative paths and overwrites duplicate REL cards; the empty-pick gate tests scratch emptiness instead of the required condition `desk dirty && rows empty`; file walkers exclude some dot-prefixed paths despite the requirement covering every relative path. Both source and packed copies need identical repairs.
Plan: Replace the walker so it compares the union of regular-file paths in livefold and the lexically newest snapshot, compares bytes via SHA-256, emits sorted `live:<relpath>` tokens, and includes hidden paths. Repair card loading to aggregate every ASSAY for each exact REL, and repair joining to match exact relative paths, deduplicate/sort assays and rows, and regenerate both outputs. Repair the gate to return nonzero exactly when the live tree differs from newest snapshot and generated rows are empty. module Walkbay

# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'json'
require_relative 'sheets'

module Bindpit
  SCRATCH = '/app/inkvat/delta.lst'
  ROSTER = '/app/inkvat/pick.json'
  LEDGER = '/app/inkvat/sieve.bin'

  module_function

  def hitch
    tokens = File.exist?(SCRATCH) ? File.read(SCRATCH).split : []
    maps = Sheets.load
    rows = tokens.map { |token| token.sub(/\A(?:live|seal):/, '') }.uniq.sort.filter_map do |rel|
      assays = maps.fetch(rel, []).uniq.sort
      next if assays.empty?

      { 'path' => "live:#{rel}", 'assays' => assays }
    end

    File.write(ROSTER, JSON.generate({ 'rows' => rows }) + "\n")
    buffer = +''.b
    rows.each do |row|
      path = row['path'].encode('UTF-8')
      buffer << [path.bytesize].pack('n') << path
      buffer << [row['assays'].length].pack('n')
      row['assays'].each do |assay|
        name = assay.encode('UTF-8')
        buffer << [name.bytesize].pack('n') << name
      end
    end
    File.binwrite(LEDGER, buffer)
    rows
  end
end

require 'digest'

module Dust
  FOLD = '/app/livefold'
  SNAP = '/app/snapurn/seals'

  module_function

  def newest_root
    name = Dir.children(SNAP).select { |entry| File.directory?(File.join(SNAP, entry)) }.sort.last
    raise 'no snapshot directory found' unless name

    File.join(SNAP, name)
  end

  def files(root)
    out = []

    Find.find(root) do |path|
      next unless File.file?(path)

      rel = path.sub(%r{\A#{Regexp.escape(root)}/?}, '')
      out << rel unless rel.empty?
    end
    out.sort
  end

  def dirty?
    snapshot = newest_root
    (files(FOLD) | files(snapshot)).any? do |rel|
      live_path = File.join(FOLD, rel)
      snap_path = File.join(snapshot, rel)
      !(File.file?(live_path) && File.file?(snap_path) &&
        Digest::SHA256.file(live_path).digest == Digest::SHA256.file(snap_path).digest)
    end
  end
end
